translation:
The bunker where the comrades had stayed was located at the colonies. It was a very poor peasant household. The living quarters were situated under one roof with the stable. The entire house consisted of one large kitchen-room, which was connected to the stable. In the kitchen stood 2 beds, a low table, and several small benches.

The entrance to the bunker was under an oven, in the ground. In this bunker were the Rosenblum family—3 persons, Yosef-Arieh Shmietanke, Yosef Vishnie, Yankev Dagerman, Yudel Voland, Motl Tabakman.

The entire Sunday passed with reports that the peasant had brought concerning scattered Polish partisans, who were murdering Jews and those who were hiding them. Despite the fact that the householder, Brankevitch, was left-leaning and pro-Jewish, he nevertheless began to waver and fear for his own family. He did not say openly that they should leave him, but it was noticeable that he was very worried. In the evening there came to us Shmuel’s brother, Yitzhak Rosenblum, Leybush Baron, Hedsheke Amne, and Malkh.
translatorNotes: “at the colonies” translates די קאלאניעס literally; the historical place reference is unclear.

Several words in the OCR are visibly corrupted or unclear; the translation preserves the apparent sense without expanding them. “Shmietanke,” “Vishnie,” “Dagerman,” “Voland,” “Tabakman,” “Brankevitch,” and “Hedsheke Amne” are conservative transliterations.
The source has an apparent inconsistency: it says “3 persons” and then lists additional individuals; this has been preserved.
